topic: Typical cabin pressurization system, Cabin pressure regulator safety v/v, outflow v/v etc.
syllabus_extract: Typical cabin pressurization system, Cabin pressure regulator safety v/v, outflow v/v etc. and its operation, Methods of sealing of cabin
specific_objectives: 17.2.2.1 Trainee will be able to understand the necessity of cabin pressurization and working principles of components.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of system schematic diagrams and identification of regulator and outflow valve components
intro_questions: Why is cabin pressurization necessary for high-altitude flight?
What are the primary sources of bleed air for the cabin system?
What happens to the cabin pressure if the outflow valve fails fully open?

development.content:
Necessity of cabin pressurization
Typical cabin pressurization system layout
Cabin pressure regulator function
Safety valve operation principles
Outflow valve control mechanisms

Methods of sealing the cabin
Pressure differential limits
Regulator safety valve interlocks
Outflow valve modes of operation
System response to altitude changes

Component failure scenarios
Emergency depressurization procedures
Maintenance access points
System testing protocols
Troubleshooting common faults

summary_questions: Explain the role of the safety valve in preventing over-pressurization.
Describe the sequence of events during an emergency depressurization.
How does the outflow valve maintain the desired cabin altitude?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note comparing the operation of the cabin pressure regulator with the air conditioning system components covered in LP 30.
